official_measurement_examples.name: Section 77 route
official_measurement_examples.fact: Section 77 provides a court-order route where a building or structure appears dangerous and works or demolition may be ordered to remove the danger.

official_measurement_examples.name: Section 78 emergency route
official_measurement_examples.fact: Section 78 allows a local authority to take necessary emergency measures where a dangerous structure requires immediate action.

official_measurement_examples.name: Section 79 distinction
official_measurement_examples.fact: Section 79 addresses ruinous or dilapidated buildings and neglected sites and must not be conflated with the immediate-danger test under section 78.

official_measurement_examples.name: Potential versus immediate danger
official_measurement_examples.fact: English council guidance consistently distinguishes potentially dangerous structures from cases requiring immediate emergency action.

official_measurement_examples.name: Cost recovery
official_measurement_examples.fact: Local-authority guidance states emergency or remedial costs may be recovered from the owner in applicable circumstances.

official_measurement_examples.name: Public safety purpose
official_measurement_examples.fact: The dangerous-structures regime is directed at removing danger to public safety, not granting a development consent.

official_measurement_examples.name: Poor condition caveat
official_measurement_examples.fact: A structure can be in poor condition without meeting the same immediate-danger threshold; the factual condition must be assessed rather than inferred from vacancy or age.

official_measurement_examples.name: Planning separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Emergency making-safe or demolition powers do not themselves grant planning permission for replacement or redevelopment.

core_rules: section 77 dangerous-structure action is not planning permission
section 78 emergency action is not planning permission
section 79 ruinous-building action is distinct from section 78 emergency action
potential danger is distinct from immediate danger
poor condition is not automatically statutory danger
vacancy is not proof of dangerous condition
emergency demolition is not redevelopment consent
making-safe works are not a planning grant
cost recovery does not determine title ownership
dangerous-structure inspection is not structural certification for future development
local-authority report response is not a parcel planning outcome
highway danger is distinct from building-control dangerous-structure powers
public-safety action does not create land rights
historic dangerous-structure action must retain its date and factual scope
no parcel dangerous-structure clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
